ticīvara.cp: . the 3 robes of a monk, viz. the inner, under, and the upper robes.
ticīvara.p: [Ti+cīvara] (na) CL=7 [Tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ samāhāroti ticīvaraṃ. Kaṅkhā, ṭī, saca. 288.] (1) (A) Three robes (Buddhist monk's lower robe, Upper robe of a monk, Double layered vestment of a Buddhist monk), A set of three robes. (B) One robe from those set of three robes (which should be determined these one robe) (Ti) (2) It has a set of three robes which should be determined, (Bhikkhu) which should determine and use a set of three robes (Ticīvarika). Ticīvara(na) [ti+ticīvara. 'ti' 2-khukiu 1-khukrvaṅaḥpru.]  A set of robe which is these three kinds of robe (means Buddhist monk's lower robe, Outer robe of a monk, Double layered vestment of a Buddhist monk), All of sum of these 3 sets of robes. There is nine pieces of robe (means three set of those three robe). Ticīvara(na) [ticīvara+dhāraṇa. cancel]. A Bhikkhu who takes and wears a set of three robes. See - Paṃsukūla.
